{{center block/s}}</noinclude><ref follow="418_3">were peculiar to the palaces of the [[Portal:Zhou dynasty|kings of ''K''âu]] in the subsequent times of the dynasty. Outside the palace were the altars appropriate to the [[w:Four Symbols|spirits of the four quarters of the land]], the 'great' or royal altar being peculiar to the kings, though the one built by Than-fû is here so named. All great undertakings, and such as required the co-operation of all the people, were preceded by a solemn sacrifice at this altar.</ref>Thus though he could not prevent the rage of his foes<ref>Referring to [[w:King Tai of Zhou|Than-fû]]'s relations with the wild hordes, described by [[Author:Mencius|Mencius]], and which obliged him to leave [[w:Bin (city)|Pin]]. As the new settlement in [[w:Predynastic Zhou|''K''âu]] grew, they did not dare to trouble it.</ref>,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He did not let fall his own fame.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The oaks and the buckthorns were (gradually) thinned,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And roads for travellers were opened.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The hordes of the {{tooltip|Khwăn|Kūn}} disappeared,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Startled and panting.

(The chiefs of) {{tooltip|Yü|Yú}} and {{tooltip|''Z''ui|Ruì}}<ref>The poet passes on here to the time of [[w:King Wen of Zhou|king Wăn]]. The story of the chiefs of [[wikt:虞|Yü]] and [[w:Rui (state)|''Z''ui]] (two states on the east of the [[w:Yellow River|Ho]]) is this:—They had a quarrel about a strip of territory, to which each of them laid claim. Going to lay their dispute before the lord of [[w:Predynastic Zhou|''K''âu]], as soon as they entered his territory, they saw the ploughers readily yielding the furrow, and travellers yielding the path, while men and women avoided one another on the road, and old people had no burdens to carry. At his court, they beheld the officers of each inferior grade giving place to those above them. They became ashamed of their own quarrel, agreed to let the disputed ground be an open territory, and withdrew without presuming to appear before Wăn. When this affair was noised abroad, more than forty states, it is said, tendered their submission to ''K''âu.</ref> were brought to an agreement{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
By king {{tooltip|Wăn|Wén}}'s stimulating their natural virtue.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Then, I may say, some came to him, previously not knowing him;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Some, drawn the last by the first;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Some, drawn by his rapid successes;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And some by his defence (of the weak) from insult.
